integrity: The proof uses only the defining witness condition. An omitted vertex \(a_i\) can be privately witnessed by \(b_j\) only if all other omitted \(A\)-vertices are confined to \(a_j\), forcing at most two omissions per side. Equality forces two omissions on each side and makes their index pairs disjoint. The resulting selected set is connected for \(n\ge4\), yielding the same ordinary and connected-super minimum layer.
scientific_limitations: The minimum-set classification is for \(\operatorname{Cr}_n\) with \(n\ge4\); the \(n=3\) boundary has additional ordinary minimum sets.
The theorem treats deletion of exactly one perfect matching from \(K_{n,n}\), not arbitrary bipartite edge deletions.
Finite exhaustive verification reaches \(n=7\) and is corroborative rather than an infinite proof.
A differently phrased or non-indexed treatment of the same crown family may exist.
title: Super and connected-super domination of crown graphs
